newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-TROUSSIER STEPS INTO NIGERIAN HOT SEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TROUSSIER STEPS INTO NIGERIAN HOT SEAT.

text.p: Frenchman Philippe Troussier will shoulder the hopes of Nigeria's World Cup campaign when he leads the country for the first time in Saturday's qualifier against Guinea.

The mild-mannered coach, dubbed the "white sorcerer" for his exploits in African soccer, will be aware that nothing but victory in the key group one game in Lagos will be enough to satisfy a fanatical public.
Nigeria trail Guinea by two points in a group they were expected to sail through. The five group winners advance to next year's finals in France.
The match is one of 10 African World Cup qualifiers being played on Saturday and Sunday -- marking the halfway mark in the final round group competition.

Troussier has been training his squad, filled with European based professionals, in Abidjan away from the frenetic atmosphere of Lagos where over-eager fans previously laid siege to the team hotel when Nigeria played their opening World Cup qualifier there in November.
Included in the squad are English-based striker Efan Ekoku, recalled for the first time in two years, and Christopher Ohenhen of Spanish club Compostella who is standing by for his debut.

Both have been brought in to beef up an attack that struggled against a modest Kenyan side in their last match in January. Nigeria were held 1-1 in Nairobi, where Kenya play host to Burkina Faso in the group's other match on Saturday.
African champions South Africa travel to Pointe Noire in the Congo for their top-of-the-table group three match on Sunday.
Lazio defender Mark Fish returns for South Africa after suspension while Congo will be without key fullbacks Elie Roch Malonga and Luc-Arsene Diamesso, who sit out after picking up two cautions.
Defeat for either Zaire or Zambia in the group's other match will mark the end of the road for the loser. Both sides have just one point from their opening two matches.
The match was switched from Kinshasa because of the raging civil war and will be played in Harare, Zimbabwe next Wednesday.
The conflict in Liberia means George Weah and his compatriots host Egypt in Accra, Ghana on Sunday, needing a win to keep their slim hopes alive.
Liberia have also been in Abidjan this week preparing for the game with Swiss-based striker Jonathan Sogbie predicting the loss of home advantage might cost his side.
"It's very difficult, especially for our home-based players. We lack the passion from the fans which is such an important factor in these games," he said.
Morocco can stretch their lead in group five if they win in Gabon on Sunday and virtually secure a fourth appearance at the World Cup finals.
Cameroon are the only other African team to have been at three World Cup finals and victory over Zimbabwe in Yaounde on Sunday will strengthen their bid.
They face a strong push from Angola, though, who play Togo in Luanda on Sunday.
Angola are exceeding even their own hopes after beating Zimbabwe last November and then drawing in Cameroon.
Other games see Namibia defend a 10-match unbeaten home record against Tunisia in Windhoek on Sunday while Ghana travel to Sierra Leone in group five.
